6º de Primaria · Inglés

Describing people and places

Ficha para imprimir
123456
1

Pregunta de arranquePiensa 30 segundos antes de seguir

«What does she look like?» y «What is she like?» parecen casi iguales. ¿Preguntan lo mismo?

Escribe o di en voz alta tu respuesta. Después .

No. What does she look like? pregunta por su aspecto: «She's tall and she has got long hair». What is she like? pregunta por su forma de ser: «She's kind and funny». Con las dos podemos hacer una descripción completa.

2

Aprende14 apartados

Para empezar: Missing: Pepper the parrot

MISSING! Have you seen Pepper?

Our parrot Pepper flew out of the window on Saturday morning, and we are very worried. Please help us to find him!

What does he look like? Pepper is a medium-sized African grey parrot. He is about thirty centimetres tall. His feathers are grey, but he has a bright red tail. He has a curved black beak and small, round, yellow eyes. He is quite old: he is twenty-five years old, but parrots can live for a very long time!

What is he like? Pepper is very friendly and talkative. He is as clever as a fox and as noisy as a fire engine. He can say «Hello, darling!», «What's for dinner?» and he can copy the sound of a phone. He is a bit shy with strangers, so please don't try to catch him. He loves sunflower seeds and grapes.

Where? He was last seen in the trees near the park on Elm Street.

If you see or hear Pepper, please call Emma on 600 123 456. There is a reward!

1. Appearance: body and face

To describe appearance (aspecto) we use be and have got. With be: «He is tall / short / medium height», «She is young / old», «They are slim / strong».

With have got: «She has got blue eyes», «He has got a beard / a moustache / freckles (pecas)». We also say «He wears glasses». En castellano: en inglés no se dice «es de ojos azules», sino «tiene ojos azules»: has got blue eyes. Y los adjetivos no tienen plural: «blue eyes», nunca «blues eyes».

2. What is she wearing?

To describe what someone has on now, we use the present continuous with wear: «She is wearing a yellow raincoat.» «They're wearing their school uniforms.» To describe what someone usually wears, we use the present simple: «My grandpa always wears a hat.»

Some useful clothes words: jumper, sweatshirt, hoodie, T-shirt, shirt, blouse, jacket, coat, raincoat, skirt, dress, trousers, jeans, shorts, trainers, boots, sandals, cap, scarf, gloves.

We can also describe patterns and materials:

  • striped (de rayas), spotted or polka-dot (de lunares), checked (de cuadros), flowery (de flores), plain (liso).
  • a woolly hat, a leather jacket, a cotton T-shirt, denim jeans.

Remember the order of adjectives: opinion, size, age, colour, pattern, material, then the noun: «a lovely long red woolly scarf», «a big old blue checked shirt».

3. Hair

For hair we usually say length, then style, then colour: long / short / medium-length, straight / wavy / curly, blond / brown / black / red / grey. «She's got long curly brown hair», «He's got short straight black hair». We can also say «He's bald» (calvo) or «She has got a ponytail» (coleta).

En castellano: hair es incontable cuando hablamos del pelo de la cabeza: «Her hair is long», no «her hairs are».

4. Personality

To describe personality (carácter) we ask What is he like?. Positive adjectives: kind (amable), friendly (simpático), funny (gracioso), clever (listo), brave (valiente), hard-working (trabajador), generous, patient, calm.

Negative ones: lazy (vago), bossy (mandón), shy (tímido, not really negative!), rude (maleducado), moody. Give an example to show it: «My grandpa is very patient: he always helps me with my homework». Consejo: usa very, quite y a bit para matizar.

5. Compound adjectives

A compound adjective is made of two words joined with a hyphen (-). They are very useful because they say a lot in a short way:

  • Appearance: blue-eyed (with blue eyes), dark-haired, long-haired, curly-haired, broad-shouldered, good-looking, well-dressed.
  • Personality: kind-hearted (very kind), easy-going (relaxed, calm), open-minded (accepts new ideas), hard-working, bad-tempered (gets angry easily), self-confident.
  • Other: left-handed, right-handed, well-known (famous), ten-year-old.

Many compound adjectives for appearance follow the pattern adjective + noun + -ed: blue + eye + -ed = blue-eyed; long + hair + -ed = long-haired.

Look at these examples:

  • «My cousin is a dark-haired, brown-eyed boy.»
  • «Our teacher is easy-going and open-minded.»
  • «I'm left-handed, like my grandma.»

Careful with ages: «She is ten years old» but «She is a ten-year-old girl» (no s when it is an adjective).

6. Adjective order

In English, adjectives go before the noun: «a big house», never «a house big». When there are several, they follow an order: opinion – size – age – shape – colour – material + noun.

«a beautiful old castle», «a small round wooden table», «a nice big red bike». En castellano: en español el adjetivo suele ir detrás («una casa grande»), por eso en inglés hay que pensar al revés. No uses más de dos o tres adjetivos seguidos.

7. Describing places

To describe a place we use there is / there are and adjectives: «My town is small and quiet. There is a beautiful beach and there are some old churches. There isn't a cinema».

Useful adjectives for places: big, small, busy (con mucha gente), quiet (tranquilo), noisy (ruidoso), modern, old, clean, dirty, crowded, peaceful. En castellano: empieza por lo general (cómo es) y luego explica qué hay.

8. As busy as a bee: similes

A simile compares two things with as … as or like. Writers use similes to make descriptions more vivid and fun. Many are fixed expressions in English:

  • as busy as a bee (muy ocupado)
  • as brave as a lion (muy valiente)
  • as quiet as a mouse (muy silencioso)
  • as cold as ice (helado)
  • as light as a feather (ligero como una pluma)
  • as strong as an ox (fuerte como un toro)
  • as slow as a snail (lento como una tortuga, ¡en inglés es un caracol!)
  • as white as snow, as green as grass, as old as the hills (muy viejo)

With like: «She runs like the wind.» «He eats like a horse.» (come muchísimo) «The room was like an oven.» (hacía mucho calor)

Notice that some similes are different in Spanish: we say «más lento que una tortuga», but in English it's a snail. And you can invent your own: «My little brother is as loud as a rock concert!»

Vídeo: Similes for Kids · Homeschool Pop (YouTube) · 717 mil visualizaciones

9. Where is it? Prepositions of place

Prepositions of place say where things are: in (dentro), on (encima), under (debajo), next to (al lado de), between (entre), behind (detrás), in front of (delante de), opposite (enfrente de), near (cerca).

«The lamp is next to the bed», «The cat is under the desk», «The bank is opposite the park», «The school is between the library and the pool». En castellano: ojo con in front of (delante) y opposite (enfrente, al otro lado).

Vídeo: In front of, behind, between: prepositions song · Maple Leaf Learning (YouTube) · 5,8 millones de visualizaciones

10. Reading: my best friend and my street

Read Adam's description: «My best friend is Sofía. She's quite tall and she has got short wavy black hair and big brown eyes. She wears glasses. She's very funny and kind, but a bit shy with new people. She lives in my street. It's a quiet street with tall trees. There's a bakery next to her house and there's a small park opposite my flat. We play there every afternoon».

11. Writing a description

Plan your description in three paragraphs (párrafos): 1) Who and appearance («My uncle Javi is tall…»), 2) personality with examples («He's very generous: he always…»), 3) place or activities («He lives in a flat near the sea…»).

Use connectors: and, but, also, because. «She's shy but very friendly», «I like him because he's funny». Consejo: relee tu texto para comprobar el orden de los adjetivos y que hayas usado has got con los ojos y el pelo.

12. Let's practise: Guess who?

Play «Guess who?» with pictures of people or classmates (with respect!). Ask only yes/no questions: «Has he got curly hair?» – «No, he hasn't». «Is she wearing a red jumper?» – «Yes, she is». «Does he wear glasses?» – «Yes, he does».

Then describe a place in the classroom without saying its name: «It's next to the window and opposite the door. There are lots of books on it». Your partner guesses: «The bookshelf!». Consejo: describe con respeto, sin palabras que puedan molestar a nadie.

13. Describing a picture

In exams and in class, you often have to describe a picture. Follow these steps:

  • 1. Say what it is in general: «This is a photo of a market.» «In this picture, I can see a family on a beach.»
  • 2. Describe the parts, using words for position: in the foreground (en primer plano), in the background (al fondo), in the middle / in the centre, on the left, on the right, at the top, at the bottom, in the top left corner.
  • 3. Describe the people with the present continuous: «On the left, there's a woman. She's wearing a red dress and she's carrying a basket.»
  • 4. Guess and give your opinion: «It might be summer because they're wearing shorts.» «They look happy.» «I think it's in Spain.» «I'd like to be there because…»

Useful phrases: There is / There are…, I can see…, It looks like…, He seems…, Maybe…, It might be…

Here is a model: «This is a photo of a busy market in a Spanish town. In the foreground, there's a fruit stall with lots of oranges and lemons. On the left, an old man is wearing a flat cap and he's choosing tomatoes. On the right, a girl in a striped dress is holding her mum's hand. In the background, I can see a church and some white houses. It might be a Saturday morning because there are a lot of people. Everybody looks relaxed. I'd like to be there because I love markets!»

Practise with a photo from a magazine: describe it to a partner without showing it, and your partner draws it. Then compare your drawing with the original photo and see how many details you got right!

Vídeo: How to Describe a Picture in English - Spoken English Lesson · Oxford Online English (YouTube) · 3,1 millones de visualizaciones

14. Famous portraits

A portrait is a picture of a person. When an artist paints himself or herself, it's a self-portrait. Here are three of the most famous portraits in the world:

  • The Mona Lisa, painted by Leonardo da Vinci in the early 16th century. It's in the Louvre museum in Paris. The woman has long dark hair and a mysterious smile. In 1911 the painting was stolen, and it was missing for more than two years! Today millions of people visit it every year.
  • Las Meninas, painted by Diego Velázquez in 1656. It's in the Prado Museum in Madrid. In the centre, there's the little princess Margarita, wearing a big white dress. Around her there are her maids, a dog and other people. On the left, Velázquez painted himself, holding his brush in front of a huge canvas.
  • Frida Kahlo's self-portraits. Frida Kahlo was a Mexican painter who painted many pictures of herself. In them, she has dark eyebrows that meet in the middle, she often wears flowers in her hair and colourful Mexican clothes, and there are often animals like monkeys and parrots around her.

Choose a portrait you like and describe it using the steps you have learned.

Vídeo: Why Is The Mona Lisa So Famous? | Story Of The Famous Painting | The Dr Binocs Show | Peekaboo Kidz · Peekaboo Kidz (YouTube) · 4,5 millones de visualizaciones

Ejemplos resueltos

Ejemplo 1. Order the words: «hair / she / got / long / blond / has».

  1. Sujeto + has got.
  2. Longitud antes que color: long blond hair.

Resultado: She has got long blond hair.

Ejemplo 2. Answer «What is your best friend like?» with two adjectives.

  1. Pregunta por el carácter, no por el aspecto.
  2. Dos adjetivos y un ejemplo.

Resultado: He's funny and generous: he always shares his snacks.

Ejemplo 3. Describe where the cat is: (debajo de la mesa, al lado de la puerta)

  1. debajo = under.
  2. al lado de = next to.

Resultado: The cat is under the table, next to the door.

Ejemplo 4. Make one compound adjective: «a girl with long hair».

  1. Pattern: adjective + noun + -ed.
  2. long + hair + -ed.

Resultado: a long-haired girl.

Ejemplo 5. Describe the position: a tree that is far away in the picture.

  1. Far away = at the back.
  2. Use «in the background».

Resultado: In the background, there's a tree.

Errores típicos

  • Poner el adjetivo detrás: «a house big» → «a big house».
  • Poner plural al adjetivo: «blues eyes» → «blue eyes».
  • Decir «hairs» para el pelo de la cabeza → «hair».
  • Confundir What is he like? (carácter) con What does he look like? (aspecto).
  • Usar is en lugar de has got: «She is blue eyes» → «She has got blue eyes».
  • Decir «a ten-years-old girl»: en el adjetivo compuesto no hay -s.
  • Confundir background (al fondo) con foreground (en primer plano).

PracticaResponde sin mirar arriba. Equivocarse aquí también enseña.

Ejercicios (24)

Hazlos en tu cuaderno y después abre la solución.

Nivel básico

  1. Translate: «Tiene el pelo corto y rizado.»

    Ver solución
    She has got short curly hair (o He has got…).

  2. Order: «car / red / a / small».

    Ver solución
    a small red car.

  3. Write the opposite: tall, quiet, lazy, old.

    Ver solución
    short, noisy, hard-working, young (o new).

  4. Translate: striped, spotted, checked.

    Ver solución
    de rayas, de lunares, de cuadros.

  5. Complete the simile: «as quiet as a ___».

    Ver solución
    mouse.

  6. Make a compound adjective: «with blue eyes».

    Ver solución
    blue-eyed.

  7. Who painted Las Meninas?

    Ver solución
    Diego Velázquez.

  8. What colour is Pepper's tail?

    Ver solución
    Red.

Nivel medio

  1. Which question asks about personality?

    Ver solución
    What is he like?

  2. Complete: «The bank is ___ the park.» (enfrente de)

    Ver solución
    opposite.

  3. Complete: «My bag is ___ my chair.» (debajo de)

    Ver solución
    under.

  4. Correct: «My sister has got browns eyes.»

    Ver solución
    My sister has got brown eyes.

  5. Complete: «There ___ two parks in my town.»

    Ver solución
    are.

  6. Describe what you are wearing today (three items with colours and patterns).

    Ver solución
    Open answer. Example: I'm wearing a blue striped T-shirt…

  7. Order the adjectives: «a (woolly / red / lovely) scarf».

    Ver solución
    a lovely red woolly scarf.

  8. Explain «easy-going» and «bad-tempered».

    Ver solución
    Easy-going: relaxed and calm. Bad-tempered: gets angry easily.

  9. Write three similes about your family or friends.

    Ver solución
    Open answer.

  10. Where is the Mona Lisa and who painted it?

    Ver solución
    In the Louvre (Paris); Leonardo da Vinci.

Nivel avanzado

  1. Describe your bedroom in two sentences.

    Ver solución
    Model answer: There is a bed next to the window. My desk is opposite the door.

  2. Describe a family member in three sentences.

    Ver solución
    Model answer: My mum is tall. She has got short brown hair. She's very kind and funny.

  3. Write a «Missing» poster for an imaginary pet with appearance, personality and similes.

    Ver solución
    Open answer.

  4. Describe a photo of your choice following the four steps.

    Ver solución
    Open answer.

  5. Describe Las Meninas: who is in the centre, on the left and in the background?

    Ver solución
    Centre: princess Margarita; left: Velázquez; background: a man in a doorway (and a mirror).

  6. Write a description of yourself using three compound adjectives.

    Ver solución
    Open answer.

¿Has nombrado estas ideas?
★

Situación de aprendizajeOur class gallery

La clase organiza una galería de retratos con descripciones en inglés, como en un museo.

Pasos

  1. Cada alumno hace un retrato o autorretrato al estilo de un artista famoso.
  2. Escribid una cartela con la descripción física, la ropa y la personalidad, con adjetivos compuestos y símiles.
  3. Preparad una audioguía describiendo el cuadro con background, foreground, left y right.
  4. Inaugurad la galería y haced de guías para las familias.

Producto final: Una galería de retratos con cartelas y audioguías en inglés.

Cómo se valora

  • Describes appearance, clothes and personality.
  • Uses compound adjectives and similes.
  • Describes the position of things in a picture.
  • Presents clearly to an audience.

Tarjetas de repasoToca la tarjeta para darle la vuelta

Según cómo respondas, la tarjeta vuelve mañana, en 3, en 7 o en 21 días.

Para familias

  • Jugad en casa a «Guess who?» con fotos de la familia, preguntando en inglés.
  • Describid juntos vuestra calle en inglés con tres frases con there is / there are.
  • Repasad juntos las tarjetas del paso 6 dos minutos al día durante una semana.

Para profesores

Saberes: Descripción física y de carácter de personas y descripción de lugares; orden del adjetivo y preposiciones de lugar (Lengua Extranjera) (RD 157/2022, tercer ciclo de Primaria).

  • «Guess who?» con personajes famosos o ilustraciones.
  • Plano del barrio con preposiciones y rutas.
  • Retrato escrito de un personaje de libro para que los compañeros lo adivinen.

Revisado el 22 de noviembre de 2026.

Qué vas a aprender

  • Describe what people look like (aspecto físico)
  • Describe personality (carácter) with adjectives
  • Describe places with there is / there are and prepositions
  • Put adjectives in the right order before the noun
  • Describe clothes and patterns with the present continuous
  • Use compound adjectives and similes in descriptions
  • Describe a picture: background, foreground, left and right
  • Talk about famous portraits

Palabras clave

What does he look like? · What is she like? · tall / short · hair · eyes · personality · adjective order · prepositions of place · there is / there are

Tiempo

80 minutos hoy + 2 minutos en cada repaso
